report_text:
Our frontend audit turned up something in jQuery 3.4.1 that I want
    triaged by the maintainers.

    When HTML from users is passed through jQuery's HTML parsing helpers
    before insertion, a crafted fragment with nested/odd closing tags can
    survive in a form that executes script in the browser. Our audit tool
    flagged it as the same class of issue as the documented jQuery XSS
    fixed in 3.5.0 (CVE-2020-11023 family). We sanitise with an allow-list
    first and still saw handler-like attributes in the output.

    Expected effect: script execution when the parsed result is inserted
    into the page. We are on 3.4.1 from npm. Can you confirm and point at
    the fixed version?
source_note:
Real public vulnerability (CVE-2020-11023, jQuery XSS via htmlPrefilter)
    reworded into end-user report style for the E2 suite. No exploit
    included. Public vulnerability; used for evaluation only.
